thread:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 router latency spike detected in eu-west-1 (auto-escalation). Alerts: p99 > 1200ms, streaming stalls observed, increased 5xx for some streaming corridors. Runbook: /runbooks/router-tail-latency
oncall-alex: I'm on it. joining bridge now -> <https://meet.redwood.co/bridge/1799999001>
sre-maya: seeing the p95 jump too, from ~120ms to ~450ms over last 10m. tail distribution looks like a second peak at ~1.4s. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/metrics/routers?region=euw1
eng-runtime-joao: any config rollout recently for routing policy? I see a canary push for lb-route-weight yesterday.
sre-maya: yes, there was a global policy change at 03:10 UTC that changed affinity weights and added a new prioritization rule for 'prefer-local' for streaming. Could be related.
incident-bot: Recent deploy metadata: deploy-id=deploy-2026-03-15-0310, author=infra-ci, changelist=lb-policy-v2.2
support-lina: support queue note: two customers reported degraded streaming experience (buffering + reconnects) in eu-west. CS tickets #7521, #7527. No data exfil.
product-ops-sam: tagging customer-impact. Any ETA on mitigation? we should notify impacted accounts.
oncall-alex: triage plan: 1) verify if misrouting/hot partitioning causing queueing 2) check per-shard load heatmap 3) consider emergency weight-balance rollback or force-eject hot shards 4) keep customers informed.
sre-maya: running quick histogram of shard p99 by router shard. query:
```
select shard_id, p99(latency_ms) from router_requests
where region='eu-west-1' and time > now() - 15m group by shard_id
```
-> top shard p99 4.2s, next few are 1.1s, rest <300ms. big skew.
eng-runtime-joao: that looks like a hotpartition. Could be routing hash skew after the new policy. Can we check routing table diffs? /svc/routerctl show-routing-config --since 2026-03-14
sre-maya: grabbed diffs. The new policy added a 'zone-affinity' multiplier that accidentally gives EUW1-primary a weight boost for certain customer tags. config diff excerpt:
```
- weight_multiplier(zone=eu-west-1)=1.0
+ weight_multiplier(zone=eu-west-1)=1.6   # unintended
```
oncall-alex: that would push more traffic to eu-west primaries and oversubscribe specific physical shards. Confirmed by heatmap.
eu1-ops-zoe: infra note: some shards in euw1 are reporting high kernel-sched wait and GPU queue backlog on inference nodes. logs show repeated requeues to secondary nodes when primary is overloaded.
sre-maya: also seeing increased streaming stall rate correlated with those shards. stack traces show long tail at router enqueue + backend backpressure.
incident-bot: customer-impact classification: high (degraded stream quality for subset of customers in eu-west). paging escalation sent to infra-leads.
oncall-alex: mitigation options:
- rollback lb-policy-v2.2 (fast, but will affect global routing)  
- adjust zone multiplier to sane value (1.1) and propagate (safer)  
- eject top hot shards and force-reshard (risky + stateful)  
- apply per-customer soft-throttle to reduce p99 (short-term)
eng-runtime-joao: quickest is to revert the multiplier to 1.0 or 1.1. I'll prepare a hotfix config and test on a canary zone first (eu-west-1a) then promote.
oncall-alex: go for canary adjust. prepare rollback if latency doesn't improve in 5m.
eng-runtime-joao: rolling config change now -> `rbctl apply --config lb-policy-v2.2-hotfix --target=eu-west-1a`
sre-maya: monitoring... p99 on canary shard dropping from 4.2s to 380ms within 90s. good signal.
eng-runtime-joao: promoting to all eu-west zones now -> `rbctl promote lb-policy-v2.2-hotfix --region=eu-west-1`
sre-maya: global euw1 p99 trending down, streaming stalls dropping, reconnect rate for affected customers halved.
oncall-alex: keep observing for 15m. if stable, we call incident mitigated and start postmortem.
product-ops-sam: notifying impacted customers via status page and CS. Notifying enterprise customers in eu-west with personalized note.
support-lina: sent CS messages to tickets #7521 and #7527 with ETA and mitigation notes.
eu1-ops-zoe: infra note: freed a couple overloaded nodes by shifting traffic, but we should schedule a follow-up for capacity rebalancing next week.
incident-bot: Alert resolved: p99 latency returned to target (p99 < 300ms) in eu-west-1. Alert cleared at 1799999178.
oncall-alex: incident summary for now: root cause = incorrect zone weight multiplier introduced in lb-policy-v2.2; caused hotpartitioning and oversubscription of specific shards leading to router enqueue/backpressure and streaming stalls. Mitigation = applied hotfix to zone multiplier and promoted to eu-west; observed p99 recovery. Next steps: postmortem, tighter deploy validation for weight multipliers, automated canary verification for routing policy changes, capacity rebalance run.
eng-runtime-joao: I'll open PR to add automated smoke tests that validate shard distribution delta after routing policy changes.
sre-maya: I'll add a monitor for sudden shard p99 skew > 3x baseline that triggers pre-emptive rollbacks.
product-ops-sam: please draft customer-facing postmortem note. include timeline and impacted customers list.
support-lina: collecting CS ticket logs and customer repros.
oncall-alex: thanks all. I'll mark this as handled and will start the incident doc. If anything regresses, ping page again.
eng-runtime-joao: one more note: while rolling the fix, noticed a secondary bug in the config parser that ignores decimal multipliers when locale is comma-based. I'll include that in the PR (likely cause of the 1.6 instead of 1.06 mis-entry in some regions).
incident-bot: Post-incident actions created: PM-1782 (postmortem), SRE-420 (monitoring rule), ENG-991 (config parser fix).
